LESSON: SONGS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMING
Topic 1.1: Songs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Songs. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do you sing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. sing alone and with others variety of simple songs in unison from different cultures and time for enjoyment,
2. clap/stamp/tap the steady beat ( pulse) when singing familiar songs to demonstrate an awareness of the beat ,
3. sing verse 1 of the Kenya national anthem in English and/or Kiswahili with proper expressive elements of music (loud, etiquette for cohesion and soft, fast, slow) while singing different peaceful co-existence, types of songs 304 Property of the Government of Kenya e) apply expressive elements of music through singing to enhance musicianship and for enjoyment, f) express ideas, feelings and emotions through singing for beat in familiar songs by tapping, effective communication, g) appreciate and enjoy singing songs from diverse cultures for cultural preservation and advancement. singing and dramatizing story and action songs guided in singing verse 1 of the Kenya National anthem paying attention to accuracy in words, rhythm and pitch songs from diverse cultural sources.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. sing alone and with others variety of simple songs in unison from different cultures and time for enjoyment,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to sing alone and with others variety of simple songs in unison from different cultures and time for enjoyment,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. clap/stamp/tap the steady beat ( pulse) when singing familiar songs to demonstrate an awareness of the beat ,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to clap/stamp/tap the steady beat ( pulse) when singing familiar songs to demonstrate an awareness of the beat ,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. sing verse 1 of the Kenya national anthem in English and/or Kiswahili with proper expressive elements of music (loud, etiquette for cohesion and soft, fast, slow) while singing different peaceful co-existence, types of songs 304 Property of the Government of Kenya e) apply expressive elements of music through singing to enhance musicianship and for enjoyment, f) express ideas, feelings and emotions through singing for beat in familiar songs by tapping, effective communication, g) appreciate and enjoy singing songs from diverse cultures for cultural preservation and advancement. singing and dramatizing story and action songs guided in singing verse 1 of the Kenya National anthem paying attention to accuracy in words, rhythm and pitch songs from diverse cultural sources.

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Songs.
2. Explain Songs to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Songs.
4. Show that you can: sing alone and with others variety of simple songs in unison from different cultures and time for enjoyment,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Songs. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why do you sing?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. sing alone and with others variety of simple songs in unison from different cultures and time for enjoyment,
2. clap/stamp/tap the steady beat ( pulse) when singing familiar songs to demonstrate an awareness of the beat ,
3. sing verse 1 of the Kenya national anthem in English and/or Kiswahili with proper expressive elements of music (loud, etiquette for cohesion and soft, fast, slow) while singing different peaceful co-existence, types of songs 304 Property of the Government of Kenya e) apply expressive elements of music through singing to enhance musicianship and for enjoyment, f) express ideas, feelings and emotions through singing for beat in familiar songs by tapping, effective communication, g) appreciate and enjoy singing songs from diverse cultures for cultural preservation and advancement. singing and dramatizing story and action songs guided in singing verse 1 of the Kenya National anthem paying attention to accuracy in words, rhythm and pitch songs from diverse cultural sources.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
